title: Session-scoped Codex thread actions still go to the profile's shared server for delegation children that own a server
outcome: Once delegation children run on an app-server of their own, session-scoped thread RPCs (fork, compact, rollback, unarchive, and the thread/list archive probes) still go through perform_codex_json_rpc_request_for(profile), i.e. the profile's shared slot. They can boot a shared server just for delegation housekeeping. If such an action reaches a non-terminal idle child whose thread is loaded on its owned server, a second server acts on the same thread. Found by the Claude reviewer of the review pair (round 1, Low) on the change that gives delegation children their own servers.
acceptance: A session-scoped thread action for a session with an attached Codex runtime goes to that session's own app-server; only a session without an attached runtime uses its profile's shared server. A behaviour test shows an owned-server child's thread action reaching its own server's wire, not the shared slot's.
